messages:
sam: Heads up: proposing a different approach to the console/analytics storage migration. Instead of per-route envelope rows, create a tiered metric_windows table with hot (last 7d) + cold (historic) partitions. Key by (route_group, tenant_id, window_start). This helps dashboard rollups + cheaper long-term storage.
anya: quick clarification: what's route_group vs route_tag?
sam: route_group is a normalized business grouping (can include multiple route_tags) so UI can aggregate at product or feature level. We'll still keep route_tag for exact lookups.
leo: main concerns: 1) queries with arbitrary JSON filters today, 2) quota checks that read current counters. 3) backfill cost.
ravi: for 1) we can't support arbitrary JSONB queries well on the TS table. Proposed fix: keep immutable envelope_events for ad-hoc search and build lightweight denorm columns in metric_windows for the most-used filters (owner, public/private, product_line). We should gather top N filters from console logs.
anya: for 2) runtime quotas need ms reads. We should maintain a current_window materialized table with single row per (tenant, route_tag) stored in redis + persisted to PG for durability. Update this from the ingest path and from scheduled reconciliation.
leo: sounds good. For backfill: run a windowed aggregator job that reads envelopes and writes to metric_windows in 15m windows with parallel workers and a global rate cap.
sam: sample DDL: 
```sql
CREATE TABLE metric_windows (
  route_group TEXT,
  route_tag TEXT,
  tenant_id UUID,
  window_start TIMESTAMP,
  requests BIGINT DEFAULT 0,
  tokens BIGINT DEFAULT 0,
  owner TEXT,
  product_line TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (route_group, tenant_id, window_start)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (window_start);
```
leo: we should avoid wide JSON columns; instead a route_meta table with route_tag -> denorm attrs. metric_windows stores route_tag and route_group only. Queries join to route_meta when needed.
ravi: dual-write plan: ingestion emits envelope_event and metric_window messages to kafka. Consumers write to PG. Keep dual-write for at least 60 days. Add a reconcile worker that samples and compares aggregates hourly.
anya: rollback playbook: stop writing to metric_windows and flip console to read envelope_events for dashboards + restore old dashboard caches. Keep reconcile metrics visible.
leo: monitoring: add prometheus metrics: metric_windows_write_latency, metric_windows_reconcile_failures, metric_windows_backfill_progress. Console should show a migration panel per-tenant with status: not-started / migrating / migrated / rollback.
sam: UX idea: staged opt-in. Console -> Admin -> Metrics migration -> "Start migration" triggers a tenant-scoped backfill & dualwrite activation. This gives customers control.
console-bot: migration feature branch passes schema-compat check: https://ci.company/metric-windows :white_check_mark:
leo: perf sims on staging: median dashboard query 120ms -> 30ms, p99 1.8s -> 380ms with route_group index and pre-joined route_meta. Backfill CPU estimate: ~48 machine-hours for 2 years of history (our numbers).
anya: sounds expensive but doable if we throttle. We'll prioritize top 10% tenants first.
ravi: action items:
- collect top UI filter fields and produce route_meta schema (anya)
- implement dual-write in ingest (leo)
- write backfill job with rate-limiter and checkpointing (ravi)
- console migration panel mock + API (ping @ben-console) (sam)
- add prometheus metrics + dashboard (infra team)
sam: schedule: prototype dualwrite on staging next Tue 09:30, run a 4hr backfill of 30d window, measure. If green -> canary 1% prod with monitoring for 24h.
leo: :+1: will add integration tests to fail if reconcile delta > 0.5% for > 1h.
anya: small ask: include a script to compute expected backfill ETA per-tenant so console can show progress estimates.
infra-bot: planned deploy of branch "metric-windows-proto" to staging at 2025-10-14T09:30Z
sam: I'll write the migration runbook and link it here when ready. No objections?
leo: none from me.
anya: none.
ravi: :white_check_mark: going to set up the reconcile job skeleton now.
